attribution.note: Zitron states the forecast in his own voice and explicitly expresses certainty.

semantics.note: The normalization preserves the definite prediction, unspecified near-term horizon, scale of AI-assisted development, and both organizational aggravating factors. Certainty is confidence, not an antecedent.

contract.note: The contract reasonably interprets service failure and difficult recovery while retaining every causal element. It fairly avoids imposing a deadline or requiring thousands of authors of one faulty change.

evidence.note: GitHub's company disclosure documents a substantial post-publication outage and recovery obstacles. It does not establish AI-assisted development at the specified scale or either organizational aggravating factor.
Amazon's company disclosure disputes attribution of earlier incidents to AI-written code. Those incidents predate the forecast, so this competing account neither fulfills nor contradicts it.

The survey was available before the cutoff and reports aggregate AI-coding incidents. It identifies no qualifying major big-tech failure or complete causal chain; it is not an independent incident finding.

reviews.rationale: The packet establishes no post-publication incident meeting all forecast elements. The documented GitHub outage lacks the required causal links, and aggregate survey responses cannot supply them. With no fixed deadline or qualifying conclusive event, the absence of a demonstrated incident does not establish failure.
